statements.impact_statement: PostgreSQL states that only major version 18 is affected and that versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-116329/. The flaw is in the statistics import functions added in PostgreSQL 18 (pg_restore_relation_stats and pg_restore_attribute_stats, src/backend/statistics/attribute_stats.c), which do not exist on the REL_16_STABLE branch. This owner publishes PostgreSQL 16 only (16.13-r0 through 16.16-r0 for Alpine 3.23), and neither function name appears in the 16.16-r0 server binary or its system catalog bootstrap file.

PostgreSQL states that only major version 18 is affected and that versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-116329/. The flaw is in the statistics import functions added in PostgreSQL 18 (pg_restore_relation_stats and pg_restore_attribute_stats, src/backend/statistics/attribute_stats.c), which do not exist on the REL_16_STABLE branch. This owner publishes PostgreSQL 16 only (16.14-r0 through 16.16-r0 for Alpine 3.24), and neither function name appears in the 16.16-r0 server binary.

CVE-2026-116329 (PostgreSQL statistics import type confusion executes arbitrary code) affects only PostgreSQL 18: the PostgreSQL security page, https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-116329/, says versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected and lists 18.7 as the only fixed release. The flaw is in pg_restore_attribute_stats, part of the statistics import functions added in PostgreSQL 18; the fix, https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/d41c9fad0856d73cc0613d322b669bf10e91dd77, changes src/backend/statistics/attribute_stats.c and is marked back-patch through 18. The PostgreSQL 17.12 source (tag REL_17_12) has no attribute_stats.c or relation_stats.c and its catalog defines neither pg_restore_attribute_stats nor pg_restore_relation_stats, and the 17.12 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.12/, do not list this CVE. The postgres server binary and the postgres.bki catalog file in every published DHI postgresql17 build for Alpine 3.23 (17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0, 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0), on both x86_64 and aarch64, contain neither function name, while the same check matches in the postgresql18 18.7 builds. Alpine's postgresql17 17.12-r0 secfixes list CVE-2026-116329 (https://security.alpinelinux.org/vuln/CVE-2026-116329), but upstream's own advisory places PostgreSQL 17 outside the affected range.

statements.status_notes: PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-116329 (PostgreSQL statistics import type confusion executes arbitrary code) in 18.7 for major version 18: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-116329/ lists 18.7 as the fixed release for 18, and the 18.7 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.7/, list this CVE. The PostgreSQL security page says versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected. The fix is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/780900dcfab7652f510ec60059cf8dbb51bfd7f5 on the REL_18_STABLE branch, tagged Security: CVE-2026-116329 and Backpatch-through: 18, in the REL_18_7 release tag and not in REL_18_6. It changes attribute_statistics_update() in src/backend/statistics/attribute_stats.c to keep the target relation open while it converts the values being imported, so that an ALTER TABLE run by user-defined code during that conversion, such as a domain's CHECK constraint, is rejected, and to raise an error if the column was dropped in the meantime; its other changes are regression tests. The DHI postgresql18 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql18 APKBUILD, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/59a1f1d230675807d5a95a0c1e57ba5d640ba039/main/postgresql18/APKBUILD, which builds the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball; none of the patches it applies touch the files this fix changes, and it lists CVE-2026-116329 under its 18.7-r0 secfixes. The DHI Alpine 3.23 package repository (x86_64 and aarch64) publishes packages built from source postgresql18 at 18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0, 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0. The vulnerable code is in the statistics import functions in the postgres server binary, /usr/libexec/postgresql18/postgres, which the postgresql18 package ships in every one of those builds on both architectures. We checked the postgres server binary in every published postgresql18 package for Alpine 3.23 on both x86_64 and aarch64 (checksums verified against the package index): 18.7-r0 reports PostgreSQL 18.7, while the earlier builds 18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0 and 18.6-r0 report 18.1, 18.2, 18.3, 18.4 and 18.6. The error message the fix adds, which ends "it was dropped during the import", is present in the postgres binary in the 18.7-r0 build and absent from it in every earlier build, on both architectures, while the existing function name attribute_statistics_update is present in every build. The earlier builds are upstream releases before 18.7, so they are affected; 18.7-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix.
